summary: @onereach/si-alert preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Vue input-alert component but its preinstall script setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a temporary directory, unzips it, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js shipped in the tarball. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-CJS bundle heavily obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style string-array rotation, hex-random identifiers, and a large integer/string table; its filename does not match the package's stated Vue-component purpose and it is not reachable from the library's Node entry point. The payload is only executable under the fetched Bun runtime, which evades scanners that inspect Node-resolved code, and its behavior cannot be recovered without executing the Bun-only bundle. The delivery mechanism — install-time fetch of an alternate language runtime whose sole purpose is to run a bundled obfuscated blob unrelated to the package's advertised functionality — is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern and results in execution of opaque code on the installer's machine during npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
